summary: Become a proficient Lead Risk Manager with ISO/IEC 27005:2022. Understand risk management frameworks to safeguard your organization’s critical data.
audienceIntro: This course is tailored for professionals who already work with information security and risk but now need to lead or significantly contribute to a formal information security risk management program aligned with ISO/IEC 27005:2022. You should be actively involved in ISMS planning, risk assessment activities, security governance, or advisory work where your decisions affect which risks are treated, accepted, shared, or avoided. This course is designed for: Information security risk managers responsible for organization‑wide ISRM programs. ISMS implementation leads aligning risk work with ISO/IEC 27001 requirements. Information security officers overseeing asset‑based risk assessments and treatment. Cybersecurity and IT risk consultants advising on ISO/IEC 27005:2022 frameworks. Risk owners accountable for information security risk acceptance decisions. IT security managers coordinating technical controls with risk treatment plans. Privacy officers handling information risk affecting personal data processing. Compliance managers maintaining ISO/IEC 27001 conformity using risk outputs. Security governance leads designing information security risk reporting to leadership. Senior analysts in information security teams supporting risk analysis and registers.
outcomes: Information Security Risk Management Program Design
modules: ISO/IEC 27005:2022 foundations and risk program setup
Risk identification, analysis, evaluation, and treatment
Risk acceptance, communication, consultation, monitoring, and review
Specialized information security risk assessment methodologies
prerequisites: To get the most value from this ISO/IEC 27005:2022 Lead Risk Manager course, you should already have a fundamental understanding of ISO/IEC 27005 and a comprehensive knowledge of risk management and information security. This includes familiarity with basic risk concepts (assets, threats, vulnerabilities, impacts, likelihood) and experience working with information security controls or ISMS activities.
